doc.title: Harold Ousley interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Chicago scene dates and racial segregation
summary: Ousley dates the Chicago scene to the late 1940s and 1950s and says clubs like the DeLisa were mixed while other areas were segregated.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So this was what years in particular for you?
Well this was, let’s see, I left for New York in ’57. DeLisa was happening in ’55, ’54, well even before then but in the ‘40s and ‘50s. Late ‘40s and ‘50s.
What was that scene like racially? Was it fully segregated or —

Well yeah, in certain areas. Now where the jazz was played, and that was well let’s see 39th Street was where The Flame was. Yeah, because at that time the music had moved from 35th Street up now to around 39th Street and 43rd. And of course you know at the DeLisa and at the clubs it was black and white. But maybe on the north side or the west side, depending on where the area was, there was segregation.
